+vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)

(* q03_heads: the attention block in two forms.  (A) the per-head cells as
   values -- a rank-3 view over the (doc.pos x heads.dim) activation, with the
   Dyalog's +.×⍤2, ⍉⍤2, MK+⍤2 and sm⍤1 as one operator or lift each, so the
   line A←sm⍤1⊢MK+⍤2⊢(Qh+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Kh)÷HD*0.5 is one Fortress line; nothing is
   copied but the products' results.  (B) round one's loop over (doc, head)
   with block views.  Both forward and the three backward products, compared
   to the last digit, then timed on the model's shape. *)
component q03_heads
export Executable
import NatReflect.{...}
import System.{...}

vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
zerosM(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(0.0)
arr3(a: ZZ32, b: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](a,b,c).fill(f)

(* ---- the elementwise algebra, generic in the index type (q01) ---- *)
opr -[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e - s)
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e / s)
opr ×[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e b[i])
exp[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => exp(e))
opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()

(* ---- row views and the row lift, over a matrix and over a rank-3 array ---- *)
object Row[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), x)
    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), x)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
row[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = Row[\r,c\](m, i)
object Row3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get((p, i, j))
    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((p, i, j), x)
    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((p, i, j), x)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
row3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = Row3[\a,b,c\](t, p, i)
nth[\nat s\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], j: ZZ32): RR64 = v[j]

rows[\nat r, nat c\](f: Any, m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = m.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](n).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): Any => f(row(m, i)))
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => nth(rs[i], j))
  end
rows[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](f: Any, t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = t.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](np n).fill(fn (k: ZZ32): Any => f(row3(t, k DIV n, k MOD n)))
    arr3(np, n, d, fn (p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => nth(rs[p n + i], j))
  end
rows[\nat r, nat c, nat r2, nat c2\](f: Any, x: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], y: Matrix[\RR64,r2,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = x.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](n).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): Any => f(row(x, i), row(y, i)))
    mat(n, d, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => nth(rs[i], j))
  end
rows[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](f: Any, x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = x.sizes
    rs = array[\Any\](np n).fill(fn (k: ZZ32): Any => f(row3(x, k DIV n, k MOD n), row3(y, k DIV n, k MOD n)))
    arr3(np, n, d, fn (p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => nth(rs[p n + i], j))
  end

(* ---- (A) the per-head cells as a rank-3 view; heads and unheads are inverse views ---- *)
(* plane d nh + h, row i, column j of the view is base[d p + i, h k + j] *)
object Heads[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32)
        extends Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.get((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.put(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.init0(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array3[\U,0,a,0,b,0,c\] = array3[\U,a,b,c\]()
end
headsOf[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32, _: N[\a\], _: N[\b\], _: N[\c\]): Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\] =
    Heads[\br,bc,a,b,c\](base, p, nh, k)
heads[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (nr, nc) = base.sizes
    headsOf(base, p, nh, k, reflect((nr DIV p) nh), reflect(p), reflect(k))
  end
(* a rank-3 array of planes (d nh + h) x p x k seen as the (d p + i, h k + j) matrix *)
object Unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,r,cc\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c)) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,cc\] = array2[\U,r,cc\]()
end
unheadsOf[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\cc\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,cc\] =
    Unheads[\a,b,c,r,cc\](base, nh)
unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, p, k) = t.sizes
    unheadsOf(t, nh, reflect((np DIV nh) p), reflect(nh k))
  end
(* ⍉⍤2 : every plane transposed, as a view *)
object T3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]) extends Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.get((p, j, i)) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.put((p, j, i), x) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.init0((p, j, i), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array3[\U,0,a,0,c,0,b\] = array3[\U,a,c,b\]()
end
opr (t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\])^T[\nat a, nat b, nat c\]: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\] = T3[\a,b,c\](t)
(* a plane as a matrix view, for the batched product *)
object Plane[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,b,c\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get((p, i, j)) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put((p, i, j), x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0((p, i, j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,b,0,c\] = array2[\U,b,c\]()
end
plane[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = Plane[\a,b,c\](t, p)
(* +.×⍤2 : the library product on each pair of planes *)
opr juxtaposition[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = x.sizes
    (yp, yn, yd) = y.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, yd).fill(0.0)
    for p <- 0#np do (plane(out, p)).assign((plane(x, p)) (plane(y, p))) end
    out
  end
(* MK +⍤2 : a matrix added to every plane *)
opr +[\nat r, nat c, nat a, nat b, nat d\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,d\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    t.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), e: RR64): RR64 => do (p, i, j) = ix; m[i,j] + e end)

(* ---- (B) round one's loop over (doc, head) with block views ---- *)
object Block[\nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]
    get(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i,j) = ij; base.get(r0 + i, c0 + j) end
    put(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.put((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    init0(ij:(ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i,j) = ij; base.init0((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
blockOf[\nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] =
    Block[\br,bc,r,c\](base, r0, c0)
block[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, nr: ZZ32, nc: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    blockOf(base, r0, c0, reflect(nr), reflect(nc))
assignInto[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](dest: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], src: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): () = do
    dest.assign(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => src[i,j])
  end

(* ---- the two vector functions and the test ---- *)
sm[\nat s\](z: Vector[\RR64,s\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do e = exp(z - (BIG MAX[t <- z] t)); e / (SUM[t <- e] t) end
sm_b[\nat s, nat t\](p: Vector[\RR64,s\], dy: Vector[\RR64,t\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = p × (dy - (p DOT dy))

maxDiff[\nat r, nat c, nat p, nat q\](a: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], b: Matrix[\RR64,p,q\]): RR64 = do
    (nr, nc) = a.sizes
    BIG MAX[i <- 0#nr, j <- 0#nc] |a[i,j] - b[i,j]|
  end

(* both forms on (bsz docs, p positions, nh heads, hd per head); returns the three max differences *)
compare(bsz: ZZ32, p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, hd: ZZ32, reps: ZZ32): () = do
    n = bsz p
    ne = nh hd
    q = mat(n, ne, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 ((3 i + 7 j) MOD 11) - 0.5)
    k = mat(n, ne, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 ((5 i + 2 j) MOD 13) - 0.6)
    v = mat(n, ne, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 ((2 i + 3 j) MOD 7) - 0.3)
    dH = mat(n, ne, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => 0.1 ((i + 5 j) MOD 9) - 0.4)
    mask = mat(p, p, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)
    scale = SQRT (1.0 hd)
    (* (A) *)
    tA0 = nanoTime()
    hcA = zerosM(n, ne)
    dQA = zerosM(n, ne)
    dKA = zerosM(n, ne)
    dVA = zerosM(n, ne)
    for rep <- seq(0#reps) do
        h(m: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = heads(m, p, nh, hd)
        u(t: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = unheads(t, nh)
        (qh, kh, vh) = (h(q), h(k), h(v))
        a = rows(sm, mask + (qh (kh^T)) / scale)
        hc = u(a vh)
        dh = h(dH)
        dVh = (a^T) dh
        dS = rows(sm_b, a, dh (vh^T)) / scale
        dQh = dS kh
        dKh = (dS^T) qh
        (dQ, dK, dV) = (u(dQh), u(dKh), u(dVh))
        assignInto(hcA, hc); assignInto(dQA, dQ); assignInto(dKA, dK); assignInto(dVA, dV)
    end
    tA1 = nanoTime()
    (* (B) *)
    hcB = zerosM(n, ne)
    dQB = zerosM(n, ne)
    dKB = zerosM(n, ne)
    dVB = zerosM(n, ne)
    for rep <- seq(0#reps) do
        att = zerosM(bsz nh p, p)
        for d <- 0#bsz, hh <- 0#nh do
            qh = block(q, d p, hh hd, p, hd); kh = block(k, d p, hh hd, p, hd); vh = block(v, d p, hh hd, p, hd)
            ah = block(att, (d nh + hh) p, 0, p, p)
            assignInto(ah, rows(sm, (qh (kh^T)) / scale + mask))
            assignInto(block(hcB, d p, hh hd, p, hd), ah vh)
        end
        for d <- 0#bsz, hh <- 0#nh do
            ah = block(att, (d nh + hh) p, 0, p, p); dh = block(dH, d p, hh hd, p, hd)
            qh = block(q, d p, hh hd, p, hd); kh = block(k, d p, hh hd, p, hd); vh = block(v, d p, hh hd, p, hd)
            assignInto(block(dVB, d p, hh hd, p, hd), (ah^T) dh)
            dS = rows(sm_b, ah, dh (vh^T)) / scale
            assignInto(block(dQB, d p, hh hd, p, hd), dS kh)
            assignInto(block(dKB, d p, hh hd, p, hd), (dS^T) qh)
        end
    end
    tB1 = nanoTime()
    println "shape docs " bsz " pos " p " heads " nh " dim " hd ", " reps " reps: (A) " ((tA1 - tA0) DIV 1000000) " ms  (B) " ((tB1 - tA1) DIV 1000000) " ms"
    println "  max |A - B|: hc " (maxDiff(hcA, hcB)) "  dQ " (maxDiff(dQA, dQB)) "  dK " (maxDiff(dKA, dKB)) "  dV " (maxDiff(dVA, dVB))
    if bsz p <= 6 then println "  hc (A) = " hcA end
  end

run(): () = do
    println "threads " (getProperty("fortress.threads", "?"))
    compare(2, 3, 2, 2, 1)
    compare(4, 16, 4, 4, 3)
  end
end

(* FlatData -- the loaders of Run C: a float parser (the library's strToFloat
   mishandles a sign and overflows on a long mantissa, ledger row 140), a
   whitespace tokenizer (String.split is a rope subdivision, row 141), text
   files as lines, vectors and matrices, and the corpus as one padded integer
   matrix with a length per document.  The check and the model share these. *)
component FlatData
export FlatData
import File.{...}

(* decimal digits, an optional '.', an optional e/E exponent; a leading '-' or '¯'.
   Digits accumulate in an RR64 mantissa, so a 17-digit mantissa is within one
   or two units in the last place of a correctly rounded parse, not exact. *)
parseFloat(s: String): RR64 = do
    neg = (s[0] = '-') OR (s[0] = '¯')
    m: RR64 := 0.0
    scale: ZZ32 := 0
    ex: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end
    seenPoint: Boolean := false
    n = |s|
    while (i < n) AND: ((s[i] =/= 'e') AND (s[i] =/= 'E')) do
        c = s[i]
        if c = '.' then seenPoint := true
        else
            m := 10.0 m + (c.codePoint - '0'.codePoint)
            if seenPoint then scale += 1 end
        end
        i += 1
    end
    if i < n then
        eneg = (s[i+1] = '-') OR (s[i+1] = '¯')
        j = if eneg OR (s[i+1] = '+') then i + 2 else i + 1 end
        ex := strToInt(s[j # (n - j)])
        if eneg then ex := -ex end
    end
    e10 = ex - scale
    r = if e10 >= 0 then m (10.0^e10)
        elif e10 >= -22 then m / (10.0^(-e10))
        else (m / (10.0^22)) / (10.0^(-e10 - 22)) end
    if neg then -r else r end
  end

(* the space-separated numbers of a line: one pass to count, one to parse *)
numbersOf(line: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    n = |line|
    cnt: ZZ32 := 0
    i: ZZ32 := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            cnt += 1
            while (i < n) AND: (line[i] =/= ' ') do i += 1 end
        end
    end
    out = array[\RR64\](cnt).fill(0.0)
    k: ZZ32 := 0
    i := 0
    while i < n do
        if line[i] = ' ' then i += 1
        else
            j: ZZ32 := i
            while (j < n) AND: (line[j] =/= ' ') do j += 1 end
            out[k] := parseFloat(line[i # (j - i)])
            k += 1
            i := j
        end
    end
    out
  end

(* the non-empty lines of a text file: one pass to count, one to read *)
readLines(path: String): Array[\String,ZZ32\] = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    cnt: ZZ32 := 0
    line: String := f.readLine()
    while |line| > 0 do cnt += 1; line := f.readLine() end
    f.close()
    g = FileReadStream(path)
    out = array[\String\](cnt).fill("")
    for i <- seq(0#cnt) do out[i] := g.readLine() end
    g.close()
    out
  end
(* one number per line *)
readVector(path: String, n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    v = array[\RR64\](n).fill(0.0)
    for i <- seq(0#n) do v[i] := parseFloat(f.readLine()) end
    f.close()
    v
  end
(* one row per line, the numbers space-separated *)
readMatrix(path: String, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    f = FileReadStream(path)
    m = array[\RR64\](rows, cols).fill(0.0)
    for i <- seq(0#rows) do
        nums = numbersOf(f.readLine())
        if |nums| =/= cols then fail("row " i " of " path " has " (|nums|) " numbers, expected " cols) end
        for j <- 0#cols do m[i, j] := nums[j] end
    end
    f.close()
    m
  end

(* the corpus as one integer matrix (documents x width): pad, the characters
   as 0..25, pad in every unused slot; and 1 + the name's length per document *)
loadCorpus(path: String, width: ZZ32, pad: ZZ32): (Array[\ZZ32,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]) = do
    names = readLines(path)
    nd = |names|
    tokm = array[\ZZ32\](nd, width).fill(pad)
    len = array[\ZZ32\](nd).fill(0)
    for d <- 0#nd do
        name = names[d]
        for j <- seq(0#|name|) do tokm[d, 1 + j] := name[j].codePoint - 'a'.codePoint end
        len[d] := 1 + |name|
    end
    (tokm, len)
  end
end

+    i: ZZ32 := if neg then 1 else 0 end

`opr` generic in the element and the shape, e.g. `opr DOT[\T extends Number, nat n\](me: Vector[\T,n\], other: T)`
(2267), one declaration per (operator, operand-shape pair), the body one
method call. Round two's declarations are the same shape with one change: they
are generic in the index type `I` of `Array[\RR64,I\]` rather than in a `nat`
per rank, so one declaration serves vectors, matrices and rank-3 arrays
(`probes/q01_algebra`).

**Absent**, and declared once in the vocabulary:

| absent | where the spec or the library promises or lacks it | declared as |
|---|---|---|
| elementwise product and quotient of two arrays | `Vector.pmul` exists (2198), `Matrix` has none (row 109), no `÷`/`×` anywhere | `opr ×`, `opr /` on `Array[\RR64,I\]` × `Array[\RR64,I\]` |
| array by scalar `/` | promised, opr-overview.tex:143–147 ("Division of a matrix or vector by a scalar may be expressed using /"), not shipped | `opr /` on `(Array[\RR64,I\], RR64)` |
| scalar extension of `+`, `-`, `MAX` | none | `(Array, RR64)` and `(RR64, Array)` pairs |
| elementwise `SQRT`, `exp`, `log` | scalar only | `opr SQRT`, `exp`, `log` on `Array[\RR64,I\]` |
| a comparison yielding a 0/1 array | none (a scalar comparison is a `Boolean`, row 41) | `opr >` on `(Array[\RR64,I\], RR64)` |
| `^T` | promised, opr-overview.tex:87–91; only `.t()` ships (row 35) | `opr (m)^T = m.t()`, and on a rank-3 array as a plane-transposing view |
| a row of a matrix as a `Vector` | `Row` (2484) extends `Array1` (row 54) | `Row`, six lines, and `Row3` for a rank-3 array |
| a lift of a vector function over rows | none | `rows(f, m)` and `rows(f, a, b)` |
| a batched product, a per-plane transpose, a matrix added to every plane | nothing above rank 2 | `opr juxtaposition` on two `Array3`s, `^T` on an `Array3`, `opr +(Matrix, Array3)` |
| a matrix as a view of a slice of a vector; a block of a matrix; a matrix as head planes and back | `subarray` gives strided sub-blocks that are not `Matrix`es | `PView`, `Block`, `Heads`, `Unheads` |
| rows at keys, one-hot, validity mask, ravel, pick, flat | none | `gather`, `onehot`, `valid`, `ravel`, `pick`, `flat` |

(* FlatArrays -- the array vocabulary of Run C, round two: what the shipped
   Vector/Matrix algebra lacks, declared once in the library's own style over
   the library's own arrays.  The inventory it was built against is the survey
   in explorations/run-c/design.md ("Round two"); nothing in that inventory is
   rewritten here.  Views take their shapes at run time through the library's
   own reflect idiom (FortressLibrary.fss:1922-1934). *)
component FlatArrays
export FlatArrays
import NatReflect.{...}
import List.{...}

(* ------------------------------------------------------- constructors ---- *)
vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
zeros(n: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(0.0)
keys(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] = array[\ZZ32\](n).fill(f)
mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)

(* ------------------------------------------- the elementwise algebra ----- *)
(* One declaration per operator, generic in the index type I, so a vector
   (I = ZZ32), a matrix ((ZZ32,ZZ32)) and a rank-3 array share it.  A scalar
   times an array is the library's juxtaposition and is not redeclared;
   + and - between two arrays of one shape are the library's. *)
opr +[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e + s)
opr +[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s + e)
opr -[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e - s)
opr -[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s - e)
opr ×[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e b[i])
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e / b[i])
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e / s)
opr MAX[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s MAX e)
opr MAX[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e MAX s)
(* a comparison on an array is a 0/1 array *)
opr >[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => if e > s then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
opr SQRT[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => SQRT e)
exp[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => exp(e))
log[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => log(e))
(* a vector on the left of a matrix scales its rows: v ×⍤0 1 m *)
opr ×[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    m.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), e: RR64): RR64 => do (i, j) = ij; v[i] e end)

(* ----------------------------------------------------- transposes -------- *)
opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()
(* the same for a call result, which may not be followed by ^T (ledger rows 144, 158) *)
transpose[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Matrix[\RR64,c,r\] = m.t()

(* ------------------------------------------------------------ views ----- *)
(* the (nr x nc) matrix at off in a flat vector, row-major *)
object PView[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](base: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(off + i c + j) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(off + i c + j, x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(off + i c + j, x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
viewAtN[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](base: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,c\] =
    PView[\s,r,c\](base, off)
viewAt[\nat s\](p: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32, nr: ZZ32, nc: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    viewAtN(p, off, reflect(nr), reflect(nc))

(* the (nr x nc) block of a matrix at (r0, c0), any numeric element type *)
object Block[\T extends Number, nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\T,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\T,r,c\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): T = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(r0 + i, c0 + j) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: T): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: T): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0((r0 + i, c0 + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,c\] = array2[\U,r,c\]()
end
blockN[\T extends Number, nat br, nat bc, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\T,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\c\]): Matrix[\T,r,c\] =
    Block[\T,br,bc,r,c\](base, r0, c0)
block[\T extends Number, nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\T,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, nr: ZZ32, nc: ZZ32): Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    blockN(base, r0, c0, reflect(nr), reflect(nc))

(* a row of a matrix, and a row of a plane of a rank-3 array, as a Vector *)
object RowView[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get(i, j)
    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), x)
    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), x)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
row[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = RowView[\r,c\](m, i)
object Row3View[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get((p, i, j))
    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((p, i, j), x)
    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((p, i, j), x)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,c\] = array1[\U,c\]()
end
row3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = Row3View[\a,b,c\](t, p, i)

(* the row-major ravel of a matrix as a vector *)
object Ravel[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\T,r,c\]) extends Vector[\T, r c\]
    get(k: ZZ32): T = base.get(k DIV c, k MOD c)
    put(k: ZZ32, x: T): () = base.put((k DIV c, k MOD c), x)
    init0(k: ZZ32, x: T): () = base.init0((k DIV c, k MOD c), x)
    replica[\U\](): Array1[\U,0,r c\] = array1[\U,r c\]()
end
ravel[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\T,r,c\]): Array[\T,ZZ32\] = Ravel[\T,r,c\](m)

(* a (docs.positions x heads.dim) activation as docs.heads planes of positions x dim:
   plane d nh + h, row i, column j is base[d p + i, h k + j]; and the inverse *)
object HeadsView[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32)
        extends Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.get((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.put(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.init0(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array3[\U,0,a,0,b,0,c\] = array3[\U,a,b,c\]()
end
headsN[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32, _: N[\a\], _: N[\b\], _: N[\c\]): Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\] =
    HeadsView[\br,bc,a,b,c\](base, p, nh, k)
heads[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (nr, nc) = base.sizes
    headsN(base, p, nh, k, reflect((nr DIV p) nh), reflect(p), reflect(k))
  end
object UnheadsView[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32)
        extends Matrix[\RR64,r,cc\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c)) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,r,0,cc\] = array2[\U,r,cc\]()
end
unheadsN[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\cc\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,cc\] =
    UnheadsView[\a,b,c,r,cc\](base, nh)
unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, p, k) = t.sizes
    unheadsN(t, nh, reflect((np DIV nh) p), reflect(nh k))
  end
(* a plane of a rank-3 array as a matrix, and every plane transposed *)
object PlaneView[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,b,c\]
    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get((p, i, j)) end
    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put((p, i, j), x) end
    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0((p, i, j), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array2[\U,0,b,0,c\] = array2[\U,b,c\]()
end
plane[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = PlaneView[\a,b,c\](t, p)
object Transposed3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]) extends Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\]
    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.get((p, j, i)) end
    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.put((p, j, i), x) end
    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (p, i, j) = ix; base.init0((p, j, i), x) end
    replica[\U\](): Array3[\U,0,a,0,c,0,b\] = array3[\U,a,c,b\]()
end
opr (t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\])^T[\nat a, nat b, nat c\]: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\] = Transposed3[\a,b,c\](t)

(* ------------------------------------------------- rank-3 algebra -------- *)
(* +.×⍤2 : the library product on every pair of planes *)
opr juxtaposition[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = x.sizes
    (yp, yn, yd) = y.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, yd)
    for p <- 0#np do (plane(out, p)).assign((plane(x, p)) (plane(y, p))) end
    out
  end
(* m +⍤2 t : a matrix added to every plane *)
opr +[\nat r, nat c, nat a, nat b, nat d\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,d\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    t.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), e: RR64): RR64 => do (p, i, j) = ix; m[i,j] + e end)

(* -------------------------------------------------- the row lift --------- *)
(* f⍤1 : f on every row of m, the results stacked; the dyadic form pairs the
   rows of two matrices; over a rank-3 array the rows are those of every plane.
   A parallel for over the rows, each written through a row view. *)
rows[\nat r, nat c\](f: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] -> Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = m.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](n, d)
    for i <- 0#n do (row(out, i)).assign(f(row(m, i))) end
    out
  end
rows[\nat r, nat c, nat r2, nat c2\](f: (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) -> Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], x: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], y: Matrix[\RR64,r2,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (n, d) = x.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](n, d)
    for i <- 0#n do (row(out, i)).assign(f(row(x, i), row(y, i))) end
    out
  end
rows[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](f: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] -> Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = t.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, d)
    for p <- 0#np, i <- 0#n do (row3(out, p, i)).assign(f(row3(t, p, i))) end
    out
  end
rows[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](f: (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) -> Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (np, n, d) = x.sizes
    out = array[\RR64\](np, n, d)
    for p <- 0#np, i <- 0#n do (row3(out, p, i)).assign(f(row3(x, p, i), row3(y, p, i))) end
    out
  end

(* ----------------------------------------------------------- keys -------- *)
(* the rows of m at the keys: m[ks;]; the elements of v at the keys: v[ks] *)
gather[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c, nat k\](m: Matrix[\T,r,c\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
    (nr, nc) = m.sizes
    array[\T\](|ks|, nc).fill(fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): T => m[ks[i], j])
  end
gather[\T extends Number, nat s, nat k\](v: Vector[\T,s\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\T,ZZ32\] =
    array[\T\](|ks|).fill(fn (i: ZZ32): T => v[ks[i]])
(* ks ∘.= ⍳width, as 0/1 *)
onehot[\nat k\](ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\], width: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(|ks|, width, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if ks[i] = j then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
(* lens ∘.> ⍳width, as 0/1: position j of row i is valid when j < lens[i] *)
valid[\nat k\](lens: Vector[\ZZ32,k\], width: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] =
    mat(|lens|, width, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j < lens[i] then 1.0 else 0.0 end)
(* ks ⌷⍤0 1 m : element ks[i] of row i *)
pick[\nat r, nat c, nat k\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
    vec(|ks|, fn (i: ZZ32): RR64 => m[i, ks[i]])
(* ⊃,/,¨ : the matrices ravelled and catenated into one vector, in order *)
flat(ms: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]...): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    out = zeros(SUM[m <- ms] |m|)
    off: ZZ32 := 0
    for m <- seq(ms) do
        (nr, nc) = m.sizes
        for i <- 0#nr, j <- 0#nc do out[off + i nc + j] := m[i,j] end
        off += nr nc
    end
    out
  end
flat(ms: List[\Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
    out = zeros(SUM[m <- ms] |m|)
    off: ZZ32 := 0
    for m <- seq(ms) do
        (nr, nc) = m.sizes
        for i <- 0#nr, j <- 0#nc do out[off + i nc + j] := m[i,j] end
        off += nr nc
    end
    out
  end
end

   per-head planes of an activation and back), the row lift, a batched product,
   and the key operations.  See explorations/run-c/design.md ("Round two"). *)
api FlatArrays
import List.{...}

(* constructors *)

keys(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]
mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

(* the elementwise algebra, one declaration per operator for every rank *)
opr +[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr +[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr -[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\]

opr ×[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr MAX[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr MAX[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr >[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\]
opr SQRT[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
exp[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
log[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\]
(* a vector on the left of a matrix scales its rows *)
opr ×[\nat s, nat r, nat c\](v: Vector[\RR64,s\], m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

(* transposes: postfix on a matrix and on every plane of a rank-3 array; a
   function for a call result, which may not be followed by ^T *)
opr (m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\])^T[\nat r, nat c\]: Matrix[\RR64,c,r\]
opr (t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\])^T[\nat a, nat b, nat c\]: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,c,0,b\]
transpose[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\]): Matrix[\RR64,c,r\]

(* views, all zero-copy, readable and writable *)
viewAt[\nat s\](p: Vector[\RR64,s\], off: ZZ32, nr: ZZ32, nc: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
block[\T extends Number, nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\T,br,bc\], r0: ZZ32, c0: ZZ32, nr: ZZ32, nc: ZZ32): Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
row[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
row3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
ravel[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\T,r,c\]): Array[\T,ZZ32\]
heads[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]
plane[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

(* the batched product and the plane-wise sum *)
opr juxtaposition[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat a2, nat b2, nat c2\](x: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], y: Array3[\RR64,0,a2,0,b2,0,c2\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

(* the row lift, monadic and dyadic, over a matrix and over a rank-3 array *)

(* keys *)
gather[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c, nat k\](m: Matrix[\T,r,c\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\T,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]

pick[\nat r, nat c, nat k\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], ks: Vector[\ZZ32,k\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
flat(ms: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]...): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]
flat(ms: List[\Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]

end

+vec(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> RR64): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = array[\RR64\](n).fill(f)
+keys(n: ZZ32, f: ZZ32 -> ZZ32): Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\] = array[\ZZ32\](n).fill(f)
+mat(r: ZZ32, c: ZZ32, f: (ZZ32,ZZ32) -> RR64): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = array[\RR64\](r,c).fill(f)
+(* One declaration per operator, generic in the index type I, so a vector
+   (I = ZZ32), a matrix ((ZZ32,ZZ32)) and a rank-3 array share it.  A scalar
+   times an array is the library's juxtaposition and is not redeclared;
+   + and - between two arrays of one shape are the library's. *)
+opr +[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e + s)
+opr +[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s + e)
+opr -[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e - s)
+opr -[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s - e)
+opr ×[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e b[i])
+opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], b: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.ivmap[\RR64\](fn (i: I, e: RR64): RR64 => e / b[i])
+opr /[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e / s)
+opr MAX[\I\](s: RR64, a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => s MAX e)
+opr MAX[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\], s: RR64): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => e MAX s)

+opr SQRT[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => SQRT e)
+exp[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => exp(e))
+log[\I\](a: Array[\RR64,I\]): Array[\RR64,I\] = a.map[\RR64\](fn (e: RR64): RR64 => log(e))

+object RowView[\nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32) extends Vector[\RR64,c\]
+    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((i, j), x)
+    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((i, j), x)
+row[\nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\RR64,r,c\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = RowView[\r,c\](m, i)

+    get(j: ZZ32): RR64 = base.get((p, i, j))
+    put(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.put((p, i, j), x)
+    init0(j: ZZ32, x: RR64): () = base.init0((p, i, j), x)
+row3[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32, i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = Row3View[\a,b,c\](t, p, i)
+(* the row-major ravel of a matrix as a vector *)
+object Ravel[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c\](base: Matrix[\T,r,c\]) extends Vector[\T, r c\]
+    get(k: ZZ32): T = base.get(k DIV c, k MOD c)
+    put(k: ZZ32, x: T): () = base.put((k DIV c, k MOD c), x)
+    init0(k: ZZ32, x: T): () = base.init0((k DIV c, k MOD c), x)
+ravel[\T extends Number, nat r, nat c\](m: Matrix[\T,r,c\]): Array[\T,ZZ32\] = Ravel[\T,r,c\](m)
+(* a (docs.positions x heads.dim) activation as docs.heads planes of positions x dim:

+object HeadsView[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32)
+    get(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.get((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j) end
+    put(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.put(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
+    init0(ix: (ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (q, i, j) = ix; base.init0(((q DIV nh) p + i, (q MOD nh) k + j), x) end
+headsN[\nat br, nat bc, nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32, _: N[\a\], _: N[\b\], _: N[\c\]): Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\] =
+heads[\nat br, nat bc\](base: Matrix[\RR64,br,bc\], p: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, k: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
+    headsN(base, p, nh, k, reflect((nr DIV p) nh), reflect(p), reflect(k))
+object UnheadsView[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32)
+    get(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32)): RR64 = do (i, j) = ij; base.get(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c)) end
+    put(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.put(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
+    init0(ij: (ZZ32,ZZ32), x: RR64): () = do (i, j) = ij; base.init0(((i DIV b) nh + (j DIV c), i MOD b, j MOD c), x) end
+unheadsN[\nat a, nat b, nat c, nat r, nat cc\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32, _: N[\r\], _: N[\cc\]): Matrix[\RR64,r,cc\] =
+unheads[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](t: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], nh: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do
+    unheadsN(t, nh, reflect((np DIV nh) p), reflect(nh k))
+(* a plane of a rank-3 array as a matrix, and every plane transposed *)
+object PlaneView[\nat a, nat b, nat c\](base: Array3[\RR64,0,a,0,b,0,c\], p: ZZ32) extends Matrix[\RR64,b,c\]

export Executable

import FlatData.{...}
import List.{...}
import System.{...}

(* --------------------------------------------------- hyperparameters ---- *)
(nEmbd, blockSize, nHead, headDim, vocabSize, bosId) = (16, 16, 4, 4, 27, 26)
(epsilon, lr0, beta1, beta2, epsilon_A, nSteps) = (10.0^(-5), 0.01, 0.85, 0.99, 10.0^(-8), 1000)

    r = SQRT (epsilon + (SUM[t <- x] t^2) / (|x|))
    y = x / r
    (dy - y ((y DOT dy) / (|y|))) / r
  end
sm_b(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = p × (dy - (p DOT dy))

        println "step " (s + 1) " loss " l "  (" ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms)"
    end
  end
end

1	(* MicroGptFlat -- microGPT in native Fortress arrays, data designed after Hsu.
2	   The model only: hyperparameters, the layout table, the four vector
3	   functions, the step, Adam and the training loop, line for line against
4	   explorations/apl/reference/hsu-flat/microgpt_concise.dyalog and the formulas
5	   (the tour: explorations/run-c/tour.md).  The array vocabulary is FlatArrays,
6	   the loaders FlatData.  Run from explorations/run-c/src: the paths are relative. *)
7	component MicroGptFlat
8	export MicroGptFlat
9	export Executable
10	import FlatArrays.{...}
11	import FlatData.{...}
12	import List.{...}
13	import System.{...}
14	
15	(* --------------------------------------------------- hyperparameters ---- *)
16	(nEmbd, blockSize, nHead, headDim, vocabSize, bosId) = (16, 16, 4, 4, 27, 26)
17	(epsilon, lr0, beta1, beta2, epsilon_A, nSteps) = (10.0^(-5), 0.01, 0.85, 0.99, 10.0^(-8), 1000)
18	(corpusPath, weightsDir) = ("../../apl/reference/dzaima/docs.txt", "../../apl/reference/dzaima/w")
19	
20	(* -------------------------------------- rmsn, sm and their backward ------ *)
21	rmsn(x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = x / SQRT (epsilon + (SUM[t <- x] t^2) / (|x|))
22	sm(z: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do e = exp(z - (BIG MAX[t <- z] t)); e / (SUM[t <- e] t) end
23	mask: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = mat(blockSize, blockSize, fn (i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 => if j > i then -(10.0^10) else 0.0 end)
24	rmsn_b(dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], x: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = do
25	    r = SQRT (epsilon + (SUM[t <- x] t^2) / (|x|))
26	    y = x / r
27	    (dy - y ((y DOT dy) / (|y|))) / r
28	  end
29	sm_b(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], dy: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] = p × (dy - (p DOT dy))
30	
31	(* ------------------------------- tactic 2/8: one vector, nine views ------ *)
32	matName(i: ZZ32): String =
33	    if i = 0 then "wte" elif i = 1 then "wpe" elif i = 2 then "lm_head" elif i = 3 then "attn_wq" elif i = 4 then "attn_wk"
34	    elif i = 5 then "attn_wv" elif i = 6 then "attn_wo" elif i = 7 then "mlp_fc1" else "mlp_fc2" end
35	matShape(i: ZZ32): (ZZ32, ZZ32) =
36	    if (i = 0) OR (i = 2) then (vocabSize, nEmbd) elif i = 7 then (4 nEmbd, nEmbd) elif i = 8 then (nEmbd, 4 nEmbd) else (nEmbd, nEmbd) end
37	matCount(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = do (r, c) = matShape(i); r c end
38	matOffset(i: ZZ32): ZZ32 = SUM[j <- 0#i] matCount(j)
39	nParams(): ZZ32 = matOffset(9)
40	loadParams(dir: String): Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] =
41	    flat(<|[\Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]\] do (r, c) = matShape(i); readMatrix(dir "/" matName(i) ".txt", r, c) end | i <- 0#9 |>)
42	view(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], i: ZZ32): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = do (r, c) = matShape(i); viewAt(p, matOffset(i), r, c) end
43	
44	(* -------------------- tactic 3/5: the corpus as one padded integer matrix - *)
45	(corpusTokens, corpusLengths) = loadCorpus(corpusPath, blockSize + 1, bosId)
46	corpus(): (Array[\ZZ32,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\], Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]) = (corpusTokens, corpusLengths)
47	nDocs(): ZZ32 = |corpusLengths|
48	
49	(* ------------------------- the step: keys -> (loss, flat gradient). Pure. -- *)
50	step(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], b: Array[\ZZ32,ZZ32\]): (RR64, Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
51	    bsz = |b|
52	    n = bsz blockSize
53	    toks = gather(corpusTokens, b)
54	    ids = ravel(block(toks, 0, 0, bsz, blockSize)); tg = ravel(block(toks, 0, 1, bsz, blockSize))
55	    vm = ravel(valid(gather(corpusLengths, b), blockSize)); nv = SUM vm; pos = keys(n, fn (r: ZZ32): ZZ32 => r MOD blockSize)
56	    (wte, wpe, lm, wq, wk, wv, wo, f1, f2) = (view(p, 0), view(p, 1), view(p, 2), view(p, 3), view(p, 4), view(p, 5), view(p, 6), view(p, 7), view(p, 8))
57	    h(m: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = heads(m, blockSize, nHead, headDim)
58	    u(t: Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32,ZZ32)\]): Array[\RR64,(ZZ32,ZZ32)\] = unheads(t, nHead)
59	    (* -- forward, all (doc, pos) rows at once -- *)
60	    x = gather(wte, ids) + gather(wpe, pos); xp = rows(rmsn, x); x1 = rows(rmsn, xp)
61	    (q, k, v) = (x1 (wq^T), x1 (wk^T), x1 (wv^T)); (qh, kh, vh) = (h(q), h(k), h(v))
62	    a = rows(sm, mask + (qh (kh^T)) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)); hc = u(a vh)
63	    x2 = xp + hc (wo^T); x3 = rows(rmsn, x2); m0 = x3 (f1^T); mr = 0.0 MAX m0; x4 = x2 + mr (f2^T)
64	    pr = rows(sm, x4 (lm^T)); loss = -(vm DOT log(pick(pr, tg))) / nv
65	    (* -- backward, one line under each forward line, bottom-up -- *)
66	    dL = (vm / nv) × (pr - onehot(tg, vocabSize)); gLM = dL^T x4; dX4 = dL lm
67	    gF2 = dX4^T mr; dM0 = (dX4 f2) × (m0 > 0.0); gF1 = dM0^T x3; dX3 = dM0 f1
68	    dX2 = dX4 + rows(rmsn_b, dX3, x2); gWO = dX2^T hc; dh = h(dX2 wo)
69	    dVh = (a^T) dh; dS = rows(sm_b, a, dh (vh^T)) / SQRT (1.0 headDim)
70	    dQh = dS kh; dKh = (dS^T) qh; (dQ, dK, dV) = (u(dQh), u(dKh), u(dVh))
71	    (gWQ, gWK, gWV) = (dQ^T x1, dK^T x1, dV^T x1); dX1 = dQ wq + dK wk + dV wv
72	    dXp = dX2 + rows(rmsn_b, dX1, xp); dX = rows(rmsn_b, dXp, x)
73	    gWTE = transpose(onehot(ids, vocabSize)) dX; gWPE = transpose(onehot(pos, blockSize)) dX
74	    (loss, flat(gWTE, gWPE, gLM, gWQ, gWK, gWV, gWO, gF1, gF2))
75	  end
76	
77	(* --------------------- Adam: three whole-vector expressions over p, m, v -- *)
78	adam(p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], g: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], t: ZZ32, lr: RR64):
79	    (Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\], Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]) = do
80	    m' = beta1 m + (1 - beta1) g
81	    v' = beta2 v + (1 - beta2) (g × g)
82	    p' = p - (lr (m' / (1 - beta1^t))) / (SQRT (v' / (1 - beta2^t)) + epsilon_A)
83	    (p', m', v')
84	  end
85	learningRate(s: ZZ32): RR64 = lr0 (1 - (1.0 s) / nSteps)
86	
87	(* --------------------------------------------------- training ----------- *)
88	run(): () = do
89	    println "microgpt flat | params " nParams() " | corpus " nDocs() " x " (blockSize + 1) " | batch 1, 5 steps"
90	    bsz = 1
91	    p: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := loadParams(weightsDir)
92	    m: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
93	    v: Array[\RR64,ZZ32\] := zeros(nParams())
94	    for s <- seq(0#5) do
95	        t0 = nanoTime()
96	        (l, g) = step(p, keys(bsz, fn (i: ZZ32): ZZ32 => (s bsz + i) MOD nDocs()))
97	        (p, m, v) := adam(p, m, v, g, s + 1, learningRate(s))
98	        println "step " (s + 1) " loss " l "  (" ((nanoTime() - t0) DIV 1000000) " ms)"
99	    end
100	  end
101	end

# Run C: microGPT in native Fortress arrays, data designed after Hsu

Round two (the tree): the model as three components, the compute side as
Fortress, line for line against the Dyalog and the formulas.

- `src/MicroGptFlat.fss` (+ `.fsi`): the model only — hyperparameters, the
  layout table, `rmsn`/`sm` and their backward at vector level, `step`, `adam`,
  the training loop; its `run()` trains five Adam steps at batch 1 from the
  committed weights and prints the losses.
- `src/FlatArrays.fss` (+ `.fsi`): the array vocabulary — the elementwise
  algebra with scalar extension as operators over the library's own arrays,
  the views (a matrix over a slice of a flat vector, a block, a row, a ravel,
  the per-head planes of an activation and back), the row lift, a batched
  product, and the key operations (`gather`, `onehot`, `valid`, `pick`,
  `flat`).
- `src/FlatData.fss` (+ `.fsi`): the loaders — a float parser, a whitespace
  tokenizer, text files as lines, vectors and matrices, the corpus as one
  padded integer matrix.
- `src/MicroGptFlatCheck.fss`: the standard of success; one line per check
  with the measured difference and PASS or FAIL, a verdict line, and a
  non-zero exit on any FAIL.
- `goldens/`: the parts of `experiment/run-c-goldens/goldens.json` the check
  reads, as text, written by `goldens/extract_goldens.py`. Unchanged.
- `checks/round2_threads1.txt`, `checks/round2_threads4.txt`: round two's
  check outputs; `checks/threads1.txt`, `threads4.txt` are round one's.
- `tour.md`, `tour.html`, `tour/`: the guided tour — for every line of the
  Dyalog, the formula, the Dyalog line, the Fortress line rendered by Fortify,
  and a note where they differ.
- `design.md`: round one's design notes and the "Round two" section — the
  survey of the shipped array algebra, the alternatives tried and rejected,
  the line budget, the subscript count, what the language gave and what had
  to be built, blinding.

  `probes/render/`). Round one's rows 140–155 are merged into the ledger.

The program and the check read the corpus and weights by paths relative to
`src/`, and the check imports the three components through the interpreter's
source path, which starts at the working directory, so run from `src/`:

source experiment/env.sh                         # JDK 25, FORTRESS_THREADS=1, -Xmx4g

The check's exit status is 0 only when every line is PASS. Its timings are in

training.

### What changed and why

Round one's data side stood (one flat vector with nine views, the corpus as
one matrix, keys, one-hot scatter-adds, masks as arithmetic, a pure step, Adam
over three vectors); its compute side was APL vocabulary with Fortress loops
inside: four row-wise functions with explicit `[i,j]` loops, elementwise
helpers, and a model that called them in the Dyalog's order. Round two splits
the program into three components and rewrites the compute side so that each
line of the model reads as its formula first and as its Dyalog line second:

- `src/FlatArrays.fss` (+`.fsi`), the vocabulary: the elementwise algebra as
  operators with scalar extension, the views, the row lift, the batched
  product, the key operations. Built against the survey below; nothing in the
  inventory is rewritten.
- `src/FlatData.fss` (+`.fsi`), the loaders: the float parser, the tokenizer,
  files as lines, vectors and matrices, the corpus. The check and the model
  share them, which removes round one's 29-line duplicate parser.
- `src/MicroGptFlat.fss` (+`.fsi`), the model only: hyperparameters, the
  layout table, `rmsn`, `sm`, `rmsn_b`, `sm_b` at vector level, `step`, `adam`,

The check imports all three and gained an aggregate verdict line and a
non-zero exit on any FAIL. The goldens did not change.

### Alternatives before committing

Each of the three places with materially different designs was tried in at
least two forms on a probe (`probes/q*.fss`, outputs beside them, renders in
`probes/render/`), compared beside its formula and its Dyalog line, and only
then written into the program.

**The row lift.** Three forms in `probes/q02_rowlift.fss`, all applying a
vector function to every row of a matrix and stacking the results:
(a) apply to row views, collect the results in an array, stack them by a
`fill`; (b) a parallel `for` over the rows, each result written through a row
view of a preallocated result; (c) a list comprehension over the rows and a
builder that stacks the list. The APL base's variant of (a), which reads the
result's rank off the first row's result by overloading, needs the function's
result type open — `Any` — and `Any` in a `nat`-generic signature is an
interpreter bug (`q02d_rankbyresult.fss`, gap row 157); it was dropped, and
the model needs no scalar-valued row function anyway. All three forms read
the same at the call, `xp = rows(rmsn, x)`, so the choice was made on cost
and on what four threads do: (b) is the cheapest at one thread and at four in
`probes/q03e_heads_rowsb.fss` against `q03_heads.fss`'s (a) (12.6 s against
13.6 s at one thread, 4.9 s against 5.4 s at four, on the attention block),
because it allocates the result uninitialised and writes each row once where
(a) fills a second array from the collected rows; (c) collects into a list
and pays the same second pass. (b) is shipped, monadic and dyadic, over a
matrix and over a rank-3 array. What made any of them possible is the row
view: a six-line object extending `Vector[\RR64,c\]` that reads and writes
through the matrix, so `rmsn`, `sm`, `rmsn_b`, `sm_b` are written once on a
vector, with no subscript, and lifted. Rejected on the way: passing the
vector functions as `nat`-generic values, which crashes the interpreter (gap
row 156) — they are written over runtime-sized arrays instead, which also
removes every static parameter from the model.

**The elementwise algebra.** (i) operators declared on the library's own
arrays, one declaration per operator generic in the index type `I` of
`Array[\RR64,I\]` (`probes/q01_algebra.fss`), against (ii) a thin wrapper
type carrying the algebra as functional methods (`q01b_wrapper.fss`). Both
work; both render the Adam update and the softmax as the formula
(`probes/render/r01_lines.png`, `r02_names.png`). (i) costs thirteen one-line
declarations for `+ - × / MAX > SQRT exp log` on vectors, matrices and
rank-3 arrays together; (ii) costs the same declarations and, beyond them,
one method per library operation the wrapper hides (`DOT`, the product,
`.t()`, `|x|`, `SUM` over the elements, subscripting), and every value in the
model would have to be wrapped and unwrapped at the views. (i) is shipped.
A third form, the APL base's per-rank spelling (one declaration per operator
per rank), was read and not tried: (i) subsumes it with a third of the lines
(gap row 162). Two things (i) could not do: a row-scaling `×` on
(vector, matrix) beside the generic `×` is rejected at declaration (gap
row 159) — the model spells it `diag(v) m`, which is the formula's spelling
anyway; and the postfix `^T` cannot be exported through an API (row 133), so
the two `^T` declarations live in the model over the vocabulary's
`transpose`.

**The attention block.** (A) the per-head cells as values — a rank-3 view
over the (doc·pos × heads·dim) activation, `+.×⍤2` as one `opr
juxtaposition` over two rank-3 arrays, `⍉⍤2` as a plane-transposing view,
`MK+⍤2` as one `opr +`, `sm⍤1` as the row lift over planes — against (B)
round one's loop over (doc, head) with block views, both in
`probes/q03_heads.fss` and its variants, compared to the last digit (every
difference 0.0) and timed on the model's shape. The judge was how close
`A←sm⍤1⊢MK+⍤2⊢(Qh+.×⍤2⊢⍉⍤2⊢Kh)÷HD*0.5` gets to one line: (A) is
`a = rows(sm, mask + (qh kh^T) / SQRT (1.0 headDim))`, one line, and the
Dyalog's four attention lines are six Fortress lines in one-to-one
correspondence with no loop and no `assignInto`; (B) is two loops of five
statements. Nothing is copied in (A) beyond what the Dyalog copies: `h` and
`u` are views (the Dyalog's reshape copies), the products allocate their
results. The price is measured in gap row 165: (A) costs 1.4× (B) at one
thread and 1.6× at four on the attention block, because every read of a
product goes through one more view level and a rank-3 `fill` costs more per
element than a rank-2 one. Four variants of (A) were timed to make sure the
price was the form's and not the spelling's: the batched product as a fill of
sums (`q03b`, slower), `h`/`u` as copies (`q03c`, the same), both (`q03d`,
slower), and the row lift in form (b) (`q03e`, 7% faster, shipped). (A) is
shipped, at about 1.1× on a whole step.

### The line budget

Code lines, blank and comment-only lines excluded (a line with code and a
trailing comment counts):

| component | round one | round two |
|---|---|---|
| `MicroGptFlat.fss` (the model) | 273 (with the loaders and the vocabulary inside) | 82 |
| `FlatArrays.fss` (the vocabulary) | — | 163 |
| `FlatData.fss` (the loaders) | — | 101 |
| `MicroGptFlatCheck.fss` | 151 | 87 |
| total | 424 | 433 |

The model was targeted at twice the Dyalog's 25 lines and is 82, of which the
step is 30 against the Dyalog's 16 and the rest 52 against 9. What stops the
rest shrinking, by line:

- the two `^T` declarations: an API cannot declare a postfix operator (ledger
  row 133, gap row 166), so they cannot live in the vocabulary;
- `matName`, 3 lines: the Dyalog reads files by index (`⎕NREAD ⍵`); the
  names are the honest price of a real loader;
- `matShape`, 2 lines, instead of the Dyalog's one-line `SHP`: a typed array
  literal at top level binds a tuple (row 142), so the shapes are a function;
- `loadParams`, 4 lines: a comprehension over the nine reads is row 96
  (`probes/q05b_listofmats.fss`), so the nine calls are spelled out;
- `rmsn_b`, 5 lines against the dfn's one: a `do` block with the dfn's three
  statements on their own lines; it could be one line and renders better as
  five (the brief's own advice);
- `corpus()` and `nDocs()`, 2 lines: accessors for the check and the driver,
  where the Dyalog reads globals;
- `adam`, 7 lines against 1: a two-line signature (three vectors in, three
  out), three body lines, the result, `end`; the Dyalog mutates globals;
- `run`, 12 lines against the driver's 1: three state variables, the loop,
  and the prints and timing the demo owes its reader;
- the four vector functions carry their `Array[\RR64,ZZ32\]` types, which
  the Dyalog's dfns do not: two are one-liners regardless.

Subscripts in the model (`[i]`, `[i,j]`, or any `[...]` that is not a static
argument or a generator clause): **0**, counted by
`grep -n "\[" src/MicroGptFlat.fss | grep -v "\[\\\\" | grep -v "SUM\[\|MAX\["`.
The layout table and the head loops, where the brief allowed subscripts, need
none: the layout is functions of the index and the head loops are gone.

### What the language gave, what had to be built this time

Given by the library, used unchanged: everything round one listed, and in
addition the prefix reduction `SUM v` over a vector (gap row 160), varargs
functions over runtime-typed matrices (row 161), top-level tuple bindings of
the hyperparameters (row 163), `fail` as a non-zero exit (row 164),
`map`/`ivmap` on every rank as the two skeletons of the algebra, `assign` on
a view as the row write of the lift, `Array3` as the storage the rank-3 views
sit on, and `Rank1`/`Rank2`/`Rank3`'s mutual exclusion as the reason the
vocabulary's overloads coexist.

Built in the vocabulary (163 lines, 14 `opr`, 10 view objects, the rest
functions): thirteen elementwise operators generic in the index type; `Diag`
and its product; `transpose` for both ranks; `PView`, `Block` (now generic in
the element type, so the corpus matrix takes it), `RowView`, `Row3View`,
`Ravel`, `HeadsView`, `UnheadsView`, `PlaneView`, `Transposed3`; the batched
product and the plane-wise sum; the row lift in four overloads; `gather` for
matrices and vectors, `onehot`, `valid`, `pick`, `flat`. Built in the loaders
(101 lines): round one's parser, one tokenizer instead of three, `readLines`,
`readVector`, `readMatrix`, `loadCorpus`. Built in the model: nothing but the
model and the two `^T` lines.

### Numerics and cost

The check's measured differences are round one's to the last digit — gradient
1.1e-16, parameters after Adam 8.3e-17, the five losses 4.4e-16 then exactly
0, batch 4 exactly 0 against the golden and against the length-weighted mean
(now weighted by the goldens' own lengths, and with the four golden
single-document losses compared, two things the review found missing), worst
finite differences 3.1e-10 and 3.7e-10 — though the summation orders differ
(`SUM[t <- x] t^2` and `x DOT dy` are the library's parallel reductions where
round one wrote index sums). Both thread counts agree with each other to the
last digit, as in round one.

Cost on this host: a batch-1 step is 5.4–5.8 s at one thread against round
one's 4.15 s on the reviewer's host of the same speed (row 154 puts the two
hosts at 1.8× apart), a batch-4 step 19 s; the check took CHECK1 s at one
thread and CHECK4 s at four, against round one's 855 and 353 on the slower
host and 451 and 226 on the reviewer's. The difference is the attention form
(gap row 165) and the lifts' row views; no speed work was done.

### Blinding

Nothing on the brief's excluded list was opened. Two things are recorded:

- Before the brief was read, the pull step ran `git log --oneline -8`. Its
  eight subject lines were this branch's: the round-two brief and its
  preparation (three subjects that paraphrase the brief), the Phase 1 review
  commit, the ledger merge, a "review probes in progress" marker, and one
  subject from the excluded `process-records/` family: "Process record 09:
  Run C (native arrays, Hsu layout) — 12 episodes, 18 dead ends, tokens and
  wall time from the transcript". Nothing in it was used, and nothing else
  of history was read.
- `CLAUDE.md`, the ledger and the Phase 1 review cite excluded paths
  (`microgpt-port.md`, `compiled-path-gaps.md`, `run-b/probes/…`,
  `run-c-review-probes/`); none was followed. `explorations/apl/base/AplCore.fss`
  and `.fsi` were read for the technique, as allowed, and not imported.
'''
s = open('design.md').read()
open('design.md', 'w').write(s.rstrip('\n') + '\n' + section)
print('design.md', len(open('design.md').read().split('\n')), 'lines')
